## Problem
`gate_enabled` (src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:79-87) returns a BARE BOOL that is `False` for TWO
materially different states:

  * the gate is genuinely turned off (a deliberate policy choice), and
  * the gate's configuration could not be READ (a fault).

Worse, the unreadable case **fails OPEN**. An unreadable or malformed config therefore silently
DISABLES the completion-verification gate, and every downstream reader — including
`_completion_precheck` — sees a state indistinguishable from an operator having turned the gate off
on purpose. A fault is laundered into a policy choice, and the gate stops protecting anything
without anyone being told.

This is a latent defect with standalone value: it is worth fixing whether or not any dependent work
is ever built.

## Approach
Return a TRI-STATE (gate on / gate off / gate config unreadable) instead of a bool, and fail CLOSED
on unreadable rather than open. Fix it at the SOURCE in `gate_enabled` rather than recomputing the
distinction at each call site — a second config read in a second place is a copy that will drift out
of sync with the first.

Update all callers to handle the third state explicitly rather than defaulting it into either
existing branch.

## Acceptance Criteria
(ACs 2 and 4 amended at close 2026-08-21 to the as-landed scope recorded in this ticket's decision,
addendum, and Patchset-2 comments — see those comments for the full evidence.)
- [x] `gate_enabled` returns a three-valued result distinguishing enabled / disabled /
      config-unreadable; no caller that needs the distinction can conflate the latter two.
      Verified: `GateState` enum in src/rebar/_commands/gates.py (merged c504977aef).
- [x] AMENDED (was: fail CLOSED on unreadable): SUPERSEDED by the documented fail-open contract —
      `docs/plan-review-gate.md` records that an unreadable config fails an opt-in gate OFF with a
      warning and never auto-enables; the unreadable condition is now surfaced (distinct
      `unreadable` verdict + single stderr warning, never silent) rather than swallowed. The
      fail-closed posture question is handed back as an operator ruling, tracked in open task
      39f8-ae7c (loveydovey-preoceanic-geese). See the decision + addendum comments.
- [x] A held-out test seeds an unreadable config and asserts the gate does NOT silently disable —
      demonstrated RED before the fix (3 of 4 RED pre-fix, recorded in the Phase-2 comment with two
      defect-seeded mutation checks); re-run green at close
      (tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py, 4 passed).
- [x] AMENDED (was: no caller relying on bool truthiness): per the Patchset-2 reviewer finding, the
      landed design DELIBERATELY preserves `GateState.__bool__` compatibility (truthy for ENABLED
      only) so `if not gate_enabled(...)` sites keep byte-identical fail-open semantics. Caller
      sweep at close: exactly three production call sites — gates.py:213 handles the tri-state
      explicitly (distinct disabled/unreadable verdicts); gates.py:308 and close_precheck.py:563
      rely on the documented preserved bool compat. String-reference sweep: remaining hits are test
      monkeypatches returning bools, unaffected by the preserved compat. No conflating site found.
- [x] Existing gate on/off behaviour is unchanged for readable configs (the invariance-guard test
      passed pre-fix and post-fix; the change merged with Verified +1 CI, existing tests unmodified).

## Provenance
Split out per operator decision 2026-08-19 from `mechanical-coherent-wolverine` (23b2-1a94), where
this surfaced as plan-review R3's first blocking finding: 'gate_enabled must distinguish gate-off
from config-unreadable, or the expectation must be computed somewhere that can see the difference.
Its current fail-open bool is the blocker.' It is filed separately because the defect stands on its
own, and because wolverine cannot author its `gate_unreadable` acceptance criteria until this
tri-state's shape is settled.

Coordinate with RP-06 (`uneducated-habitual-primate`, 'Unified effective-policy discovery for review
gates'): RP-06's effective-policy snapshot should CONSUME this tri-state, not produce its own. This
was deliberately NOT folded into RP-06 so that a small, independently-landable fix is not coupled to
a large program's schedule.
